name: 93LC86CT-I_SN
title: 93AA86A/B/C, 93LC86A/B/C, 93C86A/B/C: 16 Kbit Microwire serial EEPROM
summary: A 16 Kbit serial EEPROM driven over a three-wire Microwire-compatible bus (chip select, clock, data in, data out), with self-timed erase and write and a Ready/Busy flag on DO. The A version is organised 2048 x 8, the B version 1024 x 16, and the C version selects either with its ORG pin and adds a PE pin that write-protects the array. Supply ranges are 1.8-5.5 V (93AA86), 2.5-5.5 V (93LC86) and 4.5-5.5 V (93C86). 93LC86CT-I/SN is the 93LC86C, industrial range, in the 8-lead SOIC on tape and reel.
key_figures: 16 Kbit: 2048 x 8 (A), 1024 x 16 (B), either by ORG (C)

pins.name: CS
pins.function: Chip select, active high. Low puts the part in standby and holds its control logic in reset; a programming cycle already under way still runs to the end. Must stay low at least TCSL (250 ns) between instructions.

pins.name: CLK
pins.function: Serial clock. Start bit, opcode, address and data on DI are taken on its rising edge, and read data on DO also changes on the rising edge. It may pause high or low at any point; it is ignored while CS is low.

pins.name: DI
pins.function: Serial data input for the start bit, opcode, address and write data, sampled as CLK rises.

pins.name: DO
pins.function: Serial data output. Carries read data, valid TPD after a rising CLK edge, and, while an erase or write runs, the Ready/Busy flag; high impedance otherwise and after CS falls.

pins.name: ORG
pins.function: Word-size select, 93XX86C only. High or VCC gives x16 words; low or VSS gives x8 words. Must sit at a valid logic level.

pins.name: PE
pins.function: Program enable, 93XX86C only. At VCC the array can be erased and written; at VSS all programming is blocked. Must not float.

pins.name: EP
pins.function: DFN and TDFN only: the pad under the body; tie it to VSS or leave it unconnected.

operation.text: A 16 Kbit EEPROM on a three-wire Microwire-type serial bus. The A version is fixed at 2048 words of 8 bits, the B version at 1024 words of 16 bits, and the C version picks either through its ORG pin and adds a PE pin that write-protects the whole array. 93AA86 parts run from 1.8 V to 5.5 V in the industrial range only; 93LC86 from 2.5 V to 5.5 V and 93C86 from 4.5 V to 5.5 V, each in industrial (-40 °C to +85 °C) or automotive (-40 °C to +125 °C) grades. Erase and write cycles are self-timed with a built-in erase before each write, and endurance is 1,000,000 erase/write cycles with data retention above 200 years.

The code is device, then T for tape and reel (blank for standard packing), then -I or -E for the temperature range, then /package: P PDIP 300 mil, SN SOIC 3.90 mm, ST TSSOP 4.4 mm, MS MSOP, OT SOT-23 (reel only), MC DFN 2x3x0.90 mm, MNY TDFN 2x3x0.75 mm (reel only; the Y marks a NiPdAu finish). The SOT-23 is offered for the A and B versions; the DFN and TDFN for the C version. Other packages have a matte tin Pb-free finish. 93LC86CT-I/SN is the 2.5 V part with ORG and PE, industrial range, in the SOIC on tape and reel.

Start bit, opcode, address and write data go in on DI and are latched on each rising CLK edge; read data comes out on DO, changing after the rising edge and valid TPD later. CLK can be stopped high or low anywhere in a transfer and resumed later, provided TCKH and TCKL are met. While CS is low the clock is ignored. With CS high but no start bit yet (DI low), any number of clocks can arrive without effect. No clocks are needed while a self-timed erase or write runs.

The device sees a start bit on the first rising CLK edge at which both CS and DI are high. Until then CS, CLK and DI can change freely without starting anything. After the start bit, exactly the number of clocks the instruction needs (13, 14, 22 or 29, depending on instruction and word size) must follow; the instruction executes only once every bit it needs has arrived, after which CLK and DI are ignored until the next start bit. When raising CS to begin an instruction, CLK or DI should be low at that moment.

Raising CS takes the device out of standby. Taking it low deselects the part, returns it to standby and resets its control logic; if an erase or write cycle is running it completes first, then the part drops into standby. Between consecutive instructions CS has to stay low for at least TCSL, 250 ns.

Once an erase or write cycle has started, bringing CS high again after at least TCSL shows the status on DO: low while programming continues, high when it has finished and the device can accept another instruction. If CS stays low for the whole cycle, DO stays high impedance; checked after the cycle, DO reads high. The flag stays on DO until cleared: send a start bit, then drop CS. DO returns to high impedance when CS falls.

DI and DO may be wired together, but while the leading 0 bit of a read is being output, DO drives low while the controller may still be driving A0 high; the voltage on the line is then undefined and set by the two drivers' strengths. A resistor between DI and DO limits that current.

All operations are blocked while VCC is below about 1.5 V (93AA86, 93LC86) or 3.8 V (93C86). The part powers up with erase and write disabled (EWDS), so an EWEN instruction must come before the first ERASE or WRITE; programming then stays enabled until EWDS is sent or power is removed. READ works whatever the EWEN/EWDS state. An EWDS after every write and an external 10 kΩ pull-down on CS give added protection; on the C version, PE held low prevents accidental writes.

Sets every bit of the addressed word to 1. The self-timed cycle begins on the rising CLK edge ahead of the final address bit and lasts up to TWC (5 ms for 93AA/93LC, 2 ms for 93C); status can be polled on DO.
Sets the whole array to 1s. It runs like ERASE with a different opcode, is fully self-timed, needs no clocks once started and takes up to TEC, 6 ms. VCC has to be at least 4.5 V for ERAL to work.

After the opcode and address, DO gives a dummy 0 bit and then the 8-bit or 16-bit word, each bit changing on a rising CLK edge. Holding CS high and continuing to clock steps through the following addresses, so the array can be read out in sequence.

The opcode and address are followed by 8 or 16 data bits. The self-timed cycle, an automatic erase followed by programming, begins with the final data bit's rising CLK edge and lasts up to TWC. On the C version PE must be high before that edge.

Writes the given word into every location. It includes its own erase-all, so no ERAL is needed first, but the part must be write-enabled with EWEN. No clocks are needed once the cycle starts; it lasts up to TWL, 15 ms. PE must be high before the last data bit's rising edge on the C version, and VCC has to be at least 4.5 V.
EWEN enables all erase and write instructions; EWDS disables them. Both are 13-clock (x16) or 14-clock (x8) instructions with no data and leave DO high impedance.

On the C version ORG at VCC or logic high gives x16 words and at VSS or logic low gives x8 words; it must not be left at an undefined level. PE tied to VCC allows programming and tied to VSS blocks it; it cannot float. The A version is always x8 and the B version always x16, and both are always programmable.
